description:
Advances: ancora.review

Findings: F8 (High, frontend H1). F28 (drift badge color, Medium) rides along only because it is the same rule block; F29/F60/F61 stay on ancora-d16. Individual report: 20260904-061300-frontend.md beside ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
On this very branch, `mix spec.check` against main prints `spec.check result=pass` and exits 0 while `mix spec.review` from the same commit renders a red "fail" chip. lib/ancora/review.ex:117 derives the chip from findings_delta.change_verdict.clean? (introduced == [], no severity filter) instead of the gate report assemble/5 already holds; the gate does not block on info, clean? counts it, and this branch has seven introduced info findings. ancora.review.findings_inline is a must stating the chip reflects the gate outcome, and this branch edited that exact requirement.
Fix: take the verdict chip from the gate report the review already assembled, so chip == gate verdict by construction; add `.drift` to the bad-color badge rule at lib/ancora/review/html.ex:379 so the alarming badge is red again (F28, three lines, same file). The FindingsDelta severity-resolution half (Introduced/Pre-existing panels ignoring config severities and overrides) is F42 on ancora-d16 and is NOT in scope; say so in the record.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/review_test.exs, test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs, test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate:
  1. A fixture with introduced info-only findings: the gate passes and the rendered artifact's chip reads pass. Mutation: derive the chip from clean? again; the test must fail. Also assert the converse: a fixture with an introduced error renders fail.
  2. A drift badge renders with the bad color class. Mutation: remove `.drift` from the rule; the test must fail (assert on the CSS rule text or the rendered class set, whichever the spec names).
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.review.findings_inline (or its scenario html_view_renders_green_chip) shall state the chip is the gate verdict of the same run, with a scenario where introduced findings are all info; if the scenario name promises "green chip", make the given/when/then concrete. Decision-record edit: affects entry on ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: Review.build_with_context/3 -> assemble/5 -> Html.render; prove through `mix spec.review` on a fixture and reading the HTML back, as review_test already does.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/findings_delta.ex (F42, deferred), lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/mix/tasks/**, priv/review/** vendored assets
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/review.ex, lib/ancora/review/html.ex
- test/ancora/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (substantive edit named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No change to the artifact's size budget, to the vendored assets or their SHA pins, or to the dead-anchor set (F29 deferred). Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

IMPLEMENTED
Session: 41r6-i1-adec463e
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-41r.6/codex-41r6-i1-adec463e/log

Commit: d96d42f4287938254b8f9ab74b5e43c78acd1e17
Files touched: .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md, .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md, lib/ancora/review.ex, lib/ancora/review/html.ex, test/ancora/review_test.exs
Tests added: Ancora.ReviewTest "production review command renders the gate verdict for info and error findings"; updated Ancora.ReviewTest "puts drift under watched interface and growth under test changes" with the drift bad-color assertion
Spec acknowledgment: .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md received a substantive ancora.review.findings_inline requirement and scenario edit; .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.review_artifact_contract.md records the same-run gate verdict contract; no Spec-Ack trailer used
Verification tier: change-scoped; mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix test test/ancora/review_test.exs test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs test/ancora/static/review_budget_test.exs; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; mix spec.check --base e18fa05; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: The artifact chip now uses the same gate report and verdict function as spec.check, so info-only findings render pass while errors and warnings render fail; drift badges also use the bad-color rule again. The verdict mutation produced 1 failure and the restored test produced 0; removing the drift selector produced 1 failure and restoring it produced 0. F42 severity classification remains out of scope and untouched, and every current epic lesson was checked against this diff.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS Reviewed d96d42f over e18fa05 in /Users/mz/src/ancora-41r.6. Ran only the touched file: `mix test test/ancora/review_test.exs` -> 11 tests, 0 failures. Diff to test/ is additive; no existing assertion was deleted, relaxed, or retagged. ## Per-assertion verdict ### test/ancora/review_test.exs:105 "production review command renders the gate verdict for info and error findings" Drives the REAL command. `run_mix_subprocess(["spec.review", "--root", root, ...])` (test/support/ancora_case.exs:116) execs the real `mix` binary through a wrapper against a git fixture repo, so `Mix.Tasks.Spec.Review.run/1` -> `Ancora.Review.build/2` -> `Ancora.Review.Html.render/1` -> `File.write!` all execute for real. Not a hand-built view map. Confirmed the artifact path resolves: `--output tmp/info.html` is relative, and `output_path/2` (lib/mix/tasks/spec.review.ex:55) expands it against `--root`, matching the `File.read!(Path.join(root, "tmp/info.html"))` read-back. - :126 `List.last(output_lines(info_check.stdout)) == "spec.check result=pass"` -- PASS. Exact equality on the last stdout line, the same pattern used in append_only_test.exs:135 and decision_parser_test.exs:337. Not loose. - :142 `info_html =~ "class=\"chip pass\""` -- PASS as a precise byte sequence. I grepped lib/ancora/review/html.ex: `chip` is emitted at exactly one site, `overview/1` line 51, as `"`. Every other pill on the page renders `class="badge ..."`. So a "fail" chip elsewhere cannot satisfy this, and there is no second chip to satisfy it accidentally. - :147/:148 error-side gate assertions -- PASS. `status == 1` plus `=~ "spec.check result=fail"` (substring is correct here because the fail line carries `tier=` and counts). - :164 `error_html =~ "class=\"chip fail\""` -- PASS, same precision. Both directions are covered and the pair is mutually discriminating. A chip hardcoded to "pass" fails :164; hardcoded to "fail" fails :142. The info half is the assertion that actually guards the fix, and I traced why rather than assuming. Old code was `if(findings_delta.change_verdict.clean?, do: :pass, else: :fail)`; `clean?` is literally `introduced == []` (lib/ancora/review/findings_delta.ex:30). The fixture adds requirement `billing.unverified` with no verification block, which `Ancora.Verifier` emits as `spec/requirement_unverified` (lib/ancora/verifier.ex:144), and `FindingsDelta.repo_findings/1` runs `Verifier.verify/1` over both indexes. That requirement does not exist on the base side, so it lands in `introduced`, so `clean?` is false, so the old implementation renders `chip fail` for an info-only change. The new `Verdict.pass?(gate_report)` reads `report[:errors]`/`report[:warnings]` (populated at lib/ancora/gate.ex:552) and returns pass. The info half therefore fails on the pre-change code. That is the real guard, not the error half. ### test/ancora/review_test.exs:95 drift colour rule `assert html =~ ".fail,.error,.drift{color:var(--bad)}"` -- PASS. This is the rendered stylesheet inside the emitted HTML, not a read of html.ex source. Deleting `.drift` from the rule yields `.fail,.error{color:var(--bad)}` and this assertion fails. The complementary half, that a drift badge actually carries the class, is held at :329 `count_occurrences(html, "class=\"badge drift\">drift") == 3` in the three-subject test. The pair holds. Caveat, non-blocking: the assertion pins selector ORDER, so a cosmetic reorder to `.drift,.fail,.error{...}` fails it without any behaviour change. Acceptable for a one-line inline stylesheet; worth knowing before someone tidies the CSS. ### Source-text pinning None. No assertion reads lib/ancora/review.ex or lib/ancora/review/html.ex from disk. The CSS string at :95 is rendered output that happens to be a verbatim source literal, which is unavoidable for an inline stylesheet. ### Existing tests No weakening. `git diff e18fa05..HEAD -- test/` is +73 lines, zero deletions. :94 `class="chip fail"` predates this change and still stands. ## Isolation and hygiene - `async: true` via Ancora.TestCase; per-test root and per-module MIX_BUILD_PATH both use `Ancora.TempName.cross_vm_suffix()`, so the two subprocess pairs cannot collide with concurrent tests. - No `Process.sleep`. Subprocess calls are synchronous. - Both status assertions carry `stdout <> stderr` as the failure message, so a broken fixture reports the mix output instead of `1 != 0`. ## UNVERIFIED Reachability is NOT unverified here. The file ran green, and a passing ExUnit test has executed every assertion in it, so all six assertions in the new test and the added one at :95 demonstrably ran and produced the artifact files. What reading and a green run cannot establish is DISCRIMINATION. Mutations for the verifier, expected failure named: 1. Revert lib/ancora/review.ex:118 to `if(findings_delta.change_verdict.clean?, do: :pass, else: :fail)`. Expect review_test.exs:142 to fail (chip renders fail for the info-only change). This is the load-bearing one -- my case for it above is analytic, traced through Verifier and FindingsDelta, not measured. 2. Hardcode `verdict = "pass"` in `overview/1`, lib/ancora/review/html.ex:47. Expect :164 to fail. 3. Delete `.drift` from the rule at lib/ancora/review/html.ex:379. Expect :95 to fail. 4. Delete the `drift` class from badge rendering. Expect :329 to fail. ## Gaps worth naming, none blocking - The decision text now says "errors OR WARNINGS make both fail", and the spec requirement is worded around info-only passing. No test drives the warning direction. It would not discriminate the fix (old and new code both fail on warnings), but the sentence is unguarded. A third `write_verdict_fixture_config(root, :warning)` pass asserting `chip fail` would close it cheaply, reusing the same fixture. - The fixture switches `change/missing_decision` and `tags/new_requirement_untagged` off to isolate a single info finding. That is the honest way to build an info-only change, not a dodge, but it does mean "info-only passes" is proven under a suppressed-code config rather than defaults. - One test covers both directions and spends four subprocess invocations. Given the cost of `run_mix_subprocess`, sharing the fixture is the right trade; ExUnit reports the failing line either way.

title: The review artifact's verdict chip says fail while the gate says pass
